title: Czechia – Machinery and apparatus for filtering or purifying water – 9342–Rekonstrukce pískové filtrace na CHÚV
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je zpracování a dodání dokumentační části, dodávka a následná realizace díla „9342 – Rekonstrukce pískové filtrace na CHÚV” v JE Dukovany formou dodávky „na klíč“ a provedení všech nutně vyvolaných úprav a jejich odzkoušení na dotčených zařízeních, konstrukcích a systémech. Zhotovitel provede repasování 6 ks stávajících pískových filtrů a úpravu přidružené technologie včetně výměny stávajícího ocelového potrubí a pneumatických ventilů. Konkrétně Zhotovitel demontuje a nahradí vnitřní vestavby pískových filtrů, repasuje nádoby filtrů a nahradí pískovou filtrační hmotu za nový filtrační materiál zlepšující jak technické, tak i ekonomické parametry provozu filtračního zařízení. Zhotovitel také vymění potrubí z uhlíkové oceli vně filtru za plastové potrubí, a to včetně výměny ventilové baterie filtru a osazení nového měření tlaků s místním i vzdáleným odečítáním. Součástí díla je též demontáž 2 ks pískových filtrů i se související technologií. S ohledem na provozní podmínky a zajištění kontinuity provozu bude realizace rozdělena do jednotlivých etap. Přesné vymezení předmětu veřejné zakázky a ostatní požadavky na jeho provedení včetně informací, podmínek, specifikací a ostatních údajů jsou detailně specifikovány v části 3 a 4 Zadávací dokumentace.

title: Next Gen IACMAC RFI
description: Next Gen DoD INFORMATION ANALYSIS CENTERS (IAC) MULTIPLE AWARD CONTRACT (MAC). 774 ESS releases Sources Sought notice FA8075-27-R-0001. The IACMAC will be an indefinite delivery indefinite quantity contract that provides a wide range of mission-critical Research and Development to hundreds of requiring activities throughout the DoD. Customers come from every Service, Combatant Commands, DoD labs, and other defense and federal agencies. The scope of the IACMAC is the only DoD contract established to specifically acquire customized Research and Development services across various highly specialized focus areas. It is the only DoD contract that mandates the investigation of existing Scientific and Technical Information (STI), and the reporting and sharing of the new STI generated during performance of the task orders for others to use across the Government. The purpose of this Sources Sought synopsis is assess industry capabilities to support the evolving needs of the DoD Scientific and Technology ecosystem, which will help inform the appropriate acquisition strategy of the follow-on IACMAC. The Government requests that all interested types of businesses review and respond to this notice with the Questionnaire it needs to further its acquisition planning activities. Industry may respond to this notice by completing the attached Questionnaire and submitting it to 55cons.pkc.iacmac@us.af.mil no later than 1PM Central on Tuesday, 6 October 2026. Additional materials and information should not be submitted and will not be reviewed or considered. Any responses/information submitted will be used for planning purposes only and shall not be considered as a commitment by the Government for any purpose. Responses are strictly voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the submittal of the requested information. Any information submitted in response to this announcement is subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 USC ? 552(a). The Government does not request that any proprietary information be submitted, nor shall the Government be liable for any consequential damages for any proprietary information submitted.

title: Sources Sought for the Recapitalization of the Navy�s High Voltage (230kV) Transmission Loop and all Ancillary Equipment at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR EITHER A QUOTE OR PROPOSAL, OR AN INVITATION FOR A BID. THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO RECAPITALIZE THE NAVY�S HIGH VOLTAGE (230KV) TRANSMISSION LOOP AND ALL ANCILLARY EQUIPMENT AND GEAR AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE (NSB) KINGS BAY, GEORGIA, IN COMPLIANCE WITH ALL APPLICABLE NAVAL AND UTILITY PROVIDER PHYSICAL AND CYBERSECURITY REQUIREMENTS WITH SEAMLESS COORDINATION AND SINGLE POINT OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR EXECUTION WITHOUT UNNECESSARY SERVICE DISRUPTIONS, DELAYS, OR ADVERSE IMPACTS ASSOCIATED WITH COORDINATION OF REQUIREMENTS BETWEEN BULK POWER FEED AND INTERNAL POWER DISTRIBUTION AND ALLOCATION. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of qualified and interested participants in any of the following categories: large business; small business; U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a) business development participants; SBA certified HUBZone small business concerns; service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns; veteran-owned small business (VOSB) concerns; and women-owned small business (WOSB) concerns. Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, specialized experience, security-cleared personnel, security approvals, equipment, financial capability, and cybersecurity certifications and expertise relative to the project. The project entails the wholesale recapitalization and cybersecurity hardening of the 230kV electrical power transmission loop at NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. This is a military sensitive installation key to the nuclear deterrent mission and the utility infrastructure to be recapitalized, along with all systems, must be seamlessly connected to the 230kV grid line owned and operated by Georgia Power Company (GPC). Prior experience in interconnection and coordination with the utility provider will be considered an essential requirement when vetting viable experience. Specialized capabilities currently assumed to rest solely with the utility provider are considered essential for the timely and cost-effective completion of the project without coordination delays, interoperability concerns, and unforeseen adverse impacts in the integration and management of the project execution and subsequent receipt and transmission of power to the base tenants and supported commanders. Therefore, the project is being considered for procurement under other than full and open competition as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1 with the regulated utility service provider. This acquisition may result in the award of a design-build type (DB) effort for the wholesale recapitalization and cybersecurity hardening of the high voltage transmission line and associated gear at NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. Work will include relocation of the high power loop and crossing tower across the North River to a geotechnically stable site; replacement of conductors along the primary transmission corridor ensuring cybersecurity consistent with proprietary technology of the utility provider to eliminate vulnerabilities and ensure continued provision of power leading to thermal capacity for Columbia-class shore power loads; replacement of closed circuit television (CCTV) metering transformers with fault monitoring capability; replacement of porcelain insulators, high-voltage bushings, surge arrestors, and ground-grid bonding systems ensuring compatibility with incoming power feed loads and feeds; removal of manual or gang-operated air disconnect switches at the entry bays of Substations 1 � 3; installation of smart, supervisory-controlled Motor-Operated Disconnects (MODs) and vacuum/ SF6 circuit breakers equipped with high-speed differential bus and transformer protection schemes; and wholesale modernization of substation digital protective relays utility-grade devices with full integration of encrypted Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) telemetry between Navy substation terminal units, emergency generator control points (30MW generation fleet), and the utility provider�s bulk power dispatch centers. All telemetry and relay configurations must comply with North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection (NERC CIP) standards, applicable DoD Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-010-06 for Industrial Control Systems (ICS) standards, and ad-hoc compatibility with existing utility infrastructure as determined by the agency. The anticipated period of performance is approximately 900 calendar days from award. The estimated magnitude for this procurement is between $100,000,000.00 to $250,000,000.00. Any resulting contract action will be firm-fixed-price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237130, Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction (Small Business size standard of $45.0M); or 221122, Electric Power Distribution (Small Business size standard of 1,100 employees). In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. The Government will use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement of the subject requirement. Industry will be notified of the results of the market research via the pre-solicitation/synopsis notice as applicable. Currently, GPC, is a known source that meets the Agency�s requirements. GPC owns, operates, and regulates the regional 230kV transmission grid (Colerain and Kingsland lines) delivering bulk power to NSB Kings Bay and the upgraded 230kV air switches and transformer protection devices must integrate directly into GPC�s macro-grid schemes and automated fault isolation controls. description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � B-21: Squadron Ops/Bomber Generation Squadron, Dyess AFB, Texas DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This project will construct a combined Squadron Operations and Bomber Generation Squadron Facility at Dyess Air Force Base, Texas, approximately 167,164 gross square, to support the B-21 program, with an estimated Construction Cost Limitation (CCL) of $164,651,000. A portion of this facility will be two-story construction while the remaining portion will be a high bay maintenance hangar. Construction includes reinforced concrete drilled pier foundation, structural steel frame, masonry and insulated metal panel walls, standing seam metal roof and interior finishes. Special foundation structures due to local expansive soils. Site preparation includes site grading, construction site establishment, demolition of existing pavements and demolition of underground utilities within the site. Site improvements include earthwork landscaping, concrete pads and other exterior appurtenances. Utilities include domestic and fire protection water, electrical, sanitary sewer, storm water, natural gas and communications systems, and a 588-ton HVAC capacity. Roadways, Sidewalks and Parking includes new access drives, sidewalks, truck unloading area, Government Owned Vehicle parking areas and Personally Owned Vehicle parking lots. Facilities will be designed as permanent construction in accordance with the Department of Defense Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-01, General Building Requirements. This project will comply with Department of Defense anti-terrorism/force protection requirements per Unified Facility Criteria 4-010-01, DoD Minimum Anti-terrorism Standards for Buildings. INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY Review Attached Project Information Packet (PIP): Interested firms are directed to review the attached document. This packet provides comprehensive project requirements, constraints, and the complete questionnaire reference. Submit Responses via Microsoft Forms: To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, responses to the market research questionnaire must be submitted electronically via the following link: Online Feedback Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/rvvBByEVkA Response Due Date: All electronic responses must be submitted via the online form no later than October 6, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central Time (CT). Grimes, Dianne.K.Grimes@usace.army.mil, (817) 659-6765

description: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. THE PURPOSE OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT WILL BE USED BY THE GOVERNMENT TO MAKE APPROPRIATE ACQUISITION DECISIONS. A SUBSEQUENT SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT MAY FOLLOW. RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED AS AN ADEQUATE RESPONSE TO ANY FUTURE ANNOUNCEMENT. The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Building Services (PBS) seeks vendor interests for Elevator Maintenance and Related Services at the following locations: Location 1: Kinneary US Courthouse, 85 Marconi Blvd., Columbus, OH 43215 Location 2: Bricker Federal Building, 200 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215 Location 3: Bricker Parking Garage, 200 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215 Location 4: Rice Federal Building & US Courthouse, 200 W. Second Street, Dayton, OH 45402 This project includes, but is not limited to, providing performance-based elevator maintenance services. The Contractor shall provide full elevator maintenance service, in compliance with the ASME Safety Code requirements, manufacturer's recommendations, Elevator Industry Field Employees� Safety Handbook, National Electrical Code, and all other applicable laws, regulations, rules, ordinances, codes, etc. Full maintenance service is defined as all services, repairs, inspections and testing necessary to maintain all elevators, appurtenances, and accessories in a fully operational mode at all times except for pre-scheduled downtime including all labor, parts and materials. In part, this includes maintenance and repair of door seals, light bulbs and lighting fixtures in elevator spaces (cars, hoist ways, tops and bottoms of cars, and pits), and maintaining acceptable ride quality which may require periodic evaluation and adjustment of guide rails. Reference is made to Section 8.6 of the ASME A17.1 Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, and A18.1 Safety Standard for Platform Lifts and Stairway Chairlifts, which establishes requirements that must be adhered to. The maintenance contractor must provide all tools, equipment, supplies and personnel necessary for safely performing all tests required by the ASME A17.1 Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, and A18.1 Safety Standard for Platform Lifts and Stairway Chairlifts, and the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). GSA is the AHJ. This includes inspections and tests required at six (6) month, one (1) year, three (3) year and five (5) year intervals, and any other tests determined as necessary by the CO or designee. All tests required by code will be conducted at no additional cost to the government regardless of when the testing is performed. Those wishing to identify their capability to provide the aforementioned services should respond to this announcement via email to natasha.cunningham@gsa.gov no later than Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 3:00 PM (Eastern Standard Time). Interested parties should provide the following (see the attached response form): Company Name, Company Address, Point of Contact, phone number and email address, UEI number and capability statement for the services as stated above. Additionally include; three customer references to which you have provided similar services, and your company business size pursuant to the following questions: (1) Is your business large or small, (2) If small, does your firm qualify as a small, emerging business or small disadvantaged business? (3) If disadvantaged, specify under which disadvantaged group and if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act, (4) Is your firm a certified Hubzone firm? (5) Is your firm woman-owned or operated business? (6) Is your firm a certified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small or Veteran Owned Small Business? The method of award for any future solicitation is based on past performance and price. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION OR �SOURCES SOUGHT,� SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR OFFER. INFORMATION IS TO BE PROVIDED ON A VOLUNTARY BASIS. NO ENTITLEMENT TO PAYMENT OF DIRECT OR INDIRECT COSTS OR CHARGES INCLUDING POSTAGE AND SHIPPING WILL ARISE AS A RESULT OF THE SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION.

title: POL,PPS,AASF Concord-Fuel System Repairs
description: ****This is a pre solicitation notice only and includes a draft Scope of Work.This project includes replacing the grounding and high-level shut-off valves for both F-24 tanks (Tank 1 and Tank 2), extending the tank catwalk platform, and installing a check valve on the relief discharge into Tank 2. Additionally, the scope involves installing a truck offload meter, a visual fuel flow indicator, an eyewash station, and a filter separator maintenance platform for the truck offload/fillstand, while providing integrated truck overfill prevention and ground verification systems. To complete the facility upgrades, the project also incorporates all necessary work to install protective pipe bollards for the offload/fillstand, replace the equipment shelter ground system, provide a ground verification system for offload operations, and execute the complete supply, installation, and testing of the Automatic Tank Gauging (ATG) system on fuel storage tanks 1 and 2.

The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) anticipates the issuance of a solicitation for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project titled Precast Joint Replacement at the Federal Medical Center (FMC) Butner located at Old NC Highway 75, Butner NC 27509. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Automated Chemistry/Immunochemistry Analyzer
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to Beckman Coulter, Inc. located at 250 S Kraemer Blvd, Brea, California, 92821. This requirement supports the 88th Medical Group Clinical Laboratory at Wright Patterson Air Force base (WPAFB) for a fully automated Chemistry/Immunochemistry analyzer, associated reagents and calibrator material. The system must be compatible and integrate with the MHS GENESIS / Cerner Millenium Laboratory Information System (LIS) via an Authority to Operate (ATO)-approved middleware. This middleware will interface Chemistry, Immunochemistry, and Hematology instrumentation with MHS GENESIS to ensure error-free data transmission and critical value alerting across inpatient and hospital-wide operations. Extensive market research was conducted to identify potential sources. Techniques included, but were not limited to, internet market research, review of similar procurements, input from Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), review of the Government�s minimum technical requirements, and a Sources Sought notice. The BPA justification states that no existing mandatory source has been identified that can satisfy the organization�s specific Chemistry/Immunochemistry analyzer requirements. The WPAFB 88th Medical Group requires a fully automated Chemistry/Immunochemistry analyzer that meets the minimum technical requirements established in the Statement of Work (SOW). The system must be compatible and integrate with the MHS GENESIS / Cerner Millenium Laboratory Information System (LIS) via an Authority to Operate (ATO)-approved middleware. This middleware will interface Chemistry, Immunochemistry, and Hematology instrumentation with MHS GENESIS to ensure error-free data transmission and critical value alerting across inpatient and hospital-wide operations. Utilizing a system that does not meet these requirements would not satisfy the Government�s operational and patient care needs. As part of this market research effort, a Sources Sought notice was posted on SAM.gov on 20 August 2026. Five responses were received. The 88th Medical Group completed technical evaluations and found four out of the five companies to be technically unacceptable. The evaluations identified deficiencies including wrong methodology and instrumentation, different reagents for the instrumentation, and failure to meet the compatibility requirement with middleware interfacing with the analyzers. The Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is reasonably available: Beckman Coulter, Inc. This proposed procurement will be a Sole Source under North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) 325413 �In-vitro Diagnostic Substance Manufacturing, with a size standard of 1,250 employees. The proposed source is Beckman Coulter, Inc., 250 S Kraemer Blvd, Brea, California, 92821. Submission Instructions and Points of Contact: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties who believe they can satisfy the requirements must provide a capability statement with clear and convincing evidence of their ability to do so. The statement must demonstrate the vendor's capability to provide automated blood bank instrumentation, reagents, consumables, and support services that are fully compatible with the Government�s minimum technical and operational requirements identified in the Statement of Work. A simple statement of capability is not sufficient. All responses, questions, and capability statements shall be submitted via email to the following points of contact no later than 06 October 2026 at 4:00PM EST. � Contract Specialist: Linh Jameson, linh.jameson@us.af.mil � Contracting Officer: Joshua Clymer, joshua.clymer@us.af.mil All correspondence sent via email must contain the subject line: "Intent to Sole Source- Automated Chemistry/Immunochemistry Analyzer" Be advised that emails without this exact subject line or with prohibited attachments (zip, .exe) may be blocked by network filters. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotes. A decision by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Attachments: Statement of Work (SOW) Sole Source Justification (SSJ) Redacted

description: U.S. GOVERNMENT NOTICE OF LEASE REQUIREMENT The General Services Administration (GSA) is seeking expressions of interest from owners and authorized representatives of properties meeting the following requirements: State: Mississippi City: Vicksburg Delineated Area: City Limits of Vicksburg Minimum Sq. Ft. (ABOA): 5,065 Maximum Sq. Ft. (ABOA): 5,500 Space Type: Office Parking Spaces (Total): 0 Full Term: 15 years/10 years firm Tenant Improvement Allowance: $53.06/ABOA SF Building Specific Amortized Capital (BSAC) Allowance: $12.00/ABOA SF Offered space must meet Government requirements for fire safety, accessibility, seismic, and sustainability standards per the terms of the Lease. A fully serviced lease is required. Offered space shall not be in the 1-percent-annual chance floodplain (formerly referred to as 100-year floodplain). Entities are advised to familiarize themselves with the telecommunications prohibitions outlined under Section 889 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). For more information, visit: https://acquisition.gov/FAR-Case-2019-009/889_Part_B. ************************************************************************************************ Expressions of interest must Include. Building name and address; Contact information and e-mail address of offeror�s representative; ABOA SF and rentable square feet available, identifying the specific floors and square footages; Asking full-service rental rate per ABOA SF and RSF inclusive of a standard GSA warm-lit shell; or Asking full-service rental rate per ABOA SF and RSF inclusive of a standard GSA warm-lit shell, a tenant improvement allowance of $XX/ABOA SF, and a BSAC allowance of $XX/ABOA SF; Operating costs per ABOA SF and RSF included in the full-service rates; Submission by anyone other than the owner or manager of a property must be accompanied by written consent from the ownership granting authority to the representative in providing the information to the Government. At least one public transportation stop located within 800 walkable linear feet of the public entrance. Building shall be free of asbestos containing materials. LCO discretion will be applied to deviations. Additional Requirements: 1. Space should not be located near establishments whose primary operation is the sale of alcoholic beverages, firearms sold/discharged, or where there are tenants related to drug treatment or detention facilities. 2. All contiguous space. First floor preferred, if 2 floors, require a minimum of 2 elevators. 3. Space shall be located in a professional office setting and not within close proximity to residential areas, railroad tracks or power transmission lines. 4. Columns must be at least 20 feet apart (center to center) and 20 feet from any interior wall. Expressions of Interest Due: October 6, 2026 Send Expressions of Interest to: Name/Title: Trevor Otto Email Address: trevor.otto@gsa.gov Government Contact Information: Lease Contracting Officer Trevor Otto

title: Pelkosenniemen kunnan tilintarkastuspalvelut 2027-2030 + optio 2031-2032
description: Pelkosenniemen kunnan tilintarkastuspalvelut 2027-2030 + optio 2031-2032 Pelkosenniemen kunta pyytää tarjousta kuntalain (410/2015) mukaisista tilintarkastuspalveluista. Pelkosenniemen kunta on runsaan 900 asukkaan kunta Itä-Lapissa. Kunnan tilinpäätöksen toimintakate vuonna 2025 oli 4,4 miljoonaa euroa. Pelkosenniemen kunta on ulkoistanut kirjanpito- ja palkanlaskentapalvelunsa Monetra Oulu Oy:lle. Hankinnan kohteena on kunnan hallinnon ja talouden tarkastus sekä muut lakisääteiset tilintarkastustehtävät, mukaan lukien kunnan tytäryhteisöjen tilintarkastus. Varsinainen sopimuskausi koskee tilikausien 2027-2030 tilintarkastusta. Hankintayksiköllä on oikeus ottaa käyttöön yksi (1) kahden (2) vuoden optiokausi, joka koskee tilikausien 2031-2032 tilintarkastusta. Palveluun tulee sisältyä vähintään: - kuntalain mukainen hallinnon ja talouden tarkastus; - tilinpäätöksen tarkastus; - tilintarkastuskertomuksen laatiminen; - tarkastuslautakunnan avustaminen sen tarvitsemassa laajuudessa; - osallistuminen tarvittaessa tarkastuslautakunnan kokouksiin; - tarkastushavaintojen raportointi; - muut lakisääteiset tilintarkastustehtävät. Tarkastuksen arvioitu kokonaislaajuus on noin 6-8 tarkastuspäivää vuodessa. Arvio sisältää kunnan sekä sen tytäryhteisöjen tilintarkastuksen. Arvio ei sido hankintayksikköä. Tarjoaja voi esittää oman arvionsa tarkastuspäivien määrästä, mikäli arvio perustellusta syystä poikkeaa hankintayksikön arviosta. Arviota ei huomioida tarjousvertailussa. Tarkastuslautakunta pitää 4–6 kokousta vuodessa. Vastuullinen tilintarkastaja osallistuu asiantuntijana tarkastuslautakunnan kokouksiin tarvittaessa. Tästä muodostuvat kustannukset sisältyvät edellä mainittuun 6-8 tilintarkastuksen tarkastuspäivään. Kunnan tytäryhtiöt: - Pelkosenniemen Vuokratalot Oy (0848438-8) Kunnan omistusosuus % 100 % - Kiinteistö Oy Pelkosenniemen Liikekeskus (0722814-7) Kunnan omistusosuus % 100 % - Kiinteistö Oy Huttu-Ukko (0621079-7 ) Kunnan omistusosuus 60 % - Kiinteistö Oy Huttu-Akka (0765270-6) Kunnan omistusosuus 60 % - Asunto Oy Pelkosenniemen Huttu-Tyttö (2092384-9) Kunnan omistusosuus 53,39 %,

title: M82 and M82A1 Percussion Primers
description: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island is issuing Request for Proposal, W519TC-25-R-0016, to the SAM.GOV website with a closing date of 31 August 2026. title: Advanced Tactical Parachute System (ATPS) Design Optimization - Canopy Release Assembly (CRA)
description: 1.0 Introduction The Project Manager Soldier Survivability (PM SSV), Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE), Personnel Airdrop Systems team is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of designing, developing, or providing a modernized Canopy Release Assembly (CRA). This RFI supports the Advanced Tactical Parachute System (ATPS) Design Optimization effort. The Government is seeking information on next-generation release assembly to modernize mass tactical airdrop capabilities. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. 2.0 Background The current ATPS architecture utilizes the legacy Capewell Canopy Release Assembly to allow the jumper to disconnect the main parachute canopy from the harness upon landing, mitigating the risk of being dragged by surface winds. The current fielded CRA components are identified by part numbers 11-1-7350 (female assembly) and 60J4328 (male assembly). The PdM SCIE team is pursuing an ATPS Design Optimization effort to modernize this interface to improve ergonomics, reliability under tension, and ease of actuation for the Warfighter while ensuring absolute fail-safe security during the airdrop sequence. Furthermore, the corrosion issue across the T-11 and MC-6 harness fleet has raised material concerns about the current CRA. 3.0 Technical Requirements / Information Requested The Government requests white papers and technical data packages (if available) detailing proposed replacement components for the Capewell CRA. Proposed solutions must address the following criteria: Primary Objective: Identify a functional, modernized replacement for the existing Capewell canopy release assembly (PNs 11-1-7350 and 60J4328). System Compatibility: The proposed CRA must integrate with the existing T-11 and MC-6 risers and the T-11 harness system. Riser Design: The absolute top priority for this modernization effort is maintaining structural and operational compatibility with the current riser designs. Vendors must provide engineering analysis or proof-of-concept data demonstrating how their proposed release assembly attaches to and operates with standard risers and harness without requiring comprehensive redesigns of either component. Assembly Release Requirement: The proposed release assembly must feature a Static Line style 2-stage release process. The system must require two distinct, deliberate physical actions by the paratrooper to actuate the release, thereby preventing inadvertent deployment during aircraft exit or the opening shock sequence. Material Requirement: The proposed release assembly should feature appropriate plating or other material solutions that address the corrosion issue seen across the T-11 and MC-6 harness fleet. Corrosion considerations include industry salt spray and synthetic sweat exposure tests. Load Ratings: Submission should include information on shock loading, sustained loading, and failure loading characteristics of the proposed release assembly. Industrial Capability: Submissions should address: Current or planned domestic availability in compliance with Buy America Act and/or Berry Amendment if applicable Current or planned manufacturing volume to support parachute production Projected timeframe for ramping up to full rate production Pricing: Submissions should address: Current cost estimate per set of hardware Projected cost estimate for full rate production 4.0 Submission Instructions Responses should be submitted in PDF or DOCX format and must not exceed ten (10) pages, excluding cover pages and technical data appendices (schematics, CAD drawings, etc.). Submissions must include the company name, CAGE code, point of contact, a statement regarding the Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) and Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of the proposed Canopy Release Assembly, and business size under NAICS code 314999 (All Other Miscellaneous Textile Product Mills) and NAICS code 332999 (All Other Miscellaneous Fabricated Metal Product Manufacturing). Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending responses with information on their current commercial product(s) and how they might address the Military requirement via e-mail ONLY to Mr. Eric Louglin, eric.w.loughlin.civ@army.mil, Mr. Tashfiq Salam, Tashfiq.salam.civ@army.mil, and Mr. Mark Whiteman, g.m.whiteman.civ@army.mil, no later than 29 September 2026. Responses shall provide a courtesy copy to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist points of contact included below.

title: Advanced Tactical Parachute System (ATPS) Lightweight Canopy Fabric
description: 1.0 Introduction The Project Manager Soldier Survivability (PM SSV), Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE), Personnel Airdrop Systems team is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing advanced, lightweight parachute canopy materials. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in support of the Advanced Tactical Parachute System (ATPS) Design Optimization effort. The Government seeks to identify commercially available or developmental fabrics that offer significant weight and pack-volume reductions over legacy materials. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. 2.0 Background The current ATPS heavily relies on legacy parachute fabrics designed to withstand the rigorous deployment forces associated with mass tactical airborne operations. The standard material currently utilized for the T-11 Reserve canopy is PIA-C-44378 Type IV fabric. While this material has demonstrated historical reliability, the ATPS Design Optimization initiative seeks to decrease the overall system weight and bulk burden on the Warfighter. Reducing the weight and packed volume of the reserve canopy system is a critical objective to enhance jumper mobility, aircraft egress efficiency, and overall mission effectiveness. 3.0 Technical Requirements / Information Requested Interested industry partners are requested to provide detailed technical information on proposed canopy fabrics that meet the following objectives and constraints: Primary Objective: Identify a lower-weight and lower-bulk parachute canopy material intended to serve as a direct replacement for the currently utilized PIA-C-44378 Type IV fabric. System Compatibility: Proposed fabrics must be seamlessly compatible with the design and manufacturing processes of the T-11R (Reserve) canopy assembly. Vendors must detail how their material integrates with existing T-11R suspension lines, reinforcement tapes, and packing methodologies. Performance Impact Assessment (Critical Constraint): Industry manufacturers must explicitly detail if, and how, substituting their proposed lower-weight/lower-bulk material will impact, reduce, or alter any other critical performance specifications. Submissions must include comparative data against PIA-C-44378 Type IV baseline metrics, specifically addressing: Tear strength (warp and fill) Tensile strength Air permeability (CFM) Abrasion resistance and long-term durability (UV exposure, snag-ability, etc.) Deployment shock-loading capabilities Relative weight of proposed fabric Pack volume reduction If PFAS-free, provide additional information on performance and manufacturing impacts in comparison to baseline material Seam efficiency Sew-ability Existing use data Industrial Capability: Submissions should address: Current or planned domestic availability in compliance with Berry Amendment and Buy America Act Current or planned manufacturing volume to support parachute production Projected timeframe for ramping up to full rate production Pricing: Submissions should address: Current cost estimate for 1500 linear yds of fabric (typical 48 in width) Projected cost estimate for full rate production 4.0 Submission Instructions Responses should be submitted in PDF or DOCX format and must not exceed ten (10) pages, excluding cover pages and test data appendices. Submissions must include the company name, CAGE code, point of contact, a statement regarding the Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) and Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of the proposed Lightweight Canopy Fabric, and business size under NAICS code 314999 (All Other Miscellaneous Textile Product Mills). Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending responses with information on their current commercial product(s) and how they might address the Military requirement via e-mail ONLY to Mr. Eric Louglin, eric.w.loughlin.civ@army.mil, Mr. Tashfiq Salam, Tashfiq.salam.civ@army.mil, and Mr. Mark Whiteman, g.m.whiteman.civ@army.mil, no later than 29 September 2026. Responses shall provide a courtesy copy to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist points of contact included below.

title: Denmark – Tents – Udbud af Rammeaftale vedrørende teltservice
description: Udbuddet omfatter en rammeaftale om leje af teltservice til brug for arrangementer, øvelser og events, som afvikles af Ordregiver (”Rammeaftalen”). Rammeaftalen har til formål at dække ETKs løbende behov for leje af telte og tilhørende faciliteter til Forsvarsministeriets og underliggende myndigheders etablissementer. Rammeaftalen omfatter levering af den udbudte ydelse til Ordregivers lokationer i hele Danmark, inkl. ikke-brofaste øer. Der forventes dog alene et mindre behov for levering af ydelser til ikke-brofaste øer. Rammeaftalen indgås for en 4-årig periode, og den anslåede årlige værdi udgør 35.000.000 kr. ekskl. moms – det vil sige samlet 140.000.000 kr. ekskl. moms. Rammeaftalens maksimale værdi udgør 280.000.000 kr. ekskl. moms. Rammeaftalen omfatter leje af Teltservice inklusive følgende ydelser: • Telte til events og sanitære faciliteter • Telte til indkvartering og sanitære faciliteter • Materiale (enkeltvarer), herunder (ikke udtømmende): o Kontor- og beboelsesvogne o Køle- og frysecontainere til opbevaring af mad o Teknisk udstyr (hegn, lys, varme/køl, strøm, kabler, mv.) title: Germany – Structural shell work – "Dreispitzpassage", Claire-Waldoff-Str. 1/3/5, Reinhardstraße 2, Friedrichstraße 130 A/B/C in 10117 Berlin Leistung: Rohbauarbeiten - VOEK 380-26
description: Schaffung von 44 neuen Wohnungen auf dem Grundstück der Dreispitzpassage durch Aufstockung auf die bestehende Tiefgarage mit Rückbau der Einkaufsmall, Einbau eines begrünten Innenhofes und Anpassung der angrenzenden Gebäudeteile Bauteil G in allen Geschossen und Bauteil A/B und D/E im EG und UG (siehe Übersichtsplan Bauteile). Lage und Städtebau Das Grundstück befindet sich in zentraler Lage im Bezirk Berlin - Mitte. Sieben Häuser mit eigener Erschließung und 6 oder 7 Geschossen, bilden den dreiseitigen Block entlang der Friedrichstraße, der Claire-Waldoff-Straße und der Reinhardtstraße mit der innenliegenden erdgeschossigen "Dreispitzpassage". Entlang des historisch vorhandenen Erschließungsweges zwischen Reinhardtstraße und Claire- Waldoff-Straße, im Folgenden kurz als "Spitzweg" bezeichnet, sitzt der vierte, niedrige Riegel, ein 2-geschossiges Bauteil, bestehend aus Tiefgaragenebene TG 1 im EG und Mall im 1.OG. Hier befinden sich auch die Anlieferungszone der Mall und die Zu- und Abfahrt zur Tiefgarage. Im Inneren des Blockrandes befinden sich ebenfalls eine Tiefgaragenebene TG und darüber eine Ladenebene mit natürlich belichteter, verglaster Erschließungszone. Geplant ist den eingeschossigen Riegel auf der Tiefgarage TG 1 rückzubauen und durch eine 2- 6 Geschosse hohe Aufstockung zu ersetzen. Die innenliegende Mall über Tiefgarage TG wird ebenfalls rückgebaut und durch einen begrünten Innenhof ersetzt. Kenndaten: - Grundstück "Dreispitzpassage" - Adressen: Friedrichstraße 130 A-C, Claire-Waldoff-Straße 1, 3, 5 und Reinhardtstraße 2 - Bezirk: Mitte von Berlin - Gemarkung: Berlin Mitte - Flur: 921 - Flurstück: 373 und 374 - Flächengröße: 7373 m² - Mittlere Geländehöhe: ca. 33,50 m ü.NN Neubau - Aufstockung: Der neue Baukörper beginnt oberhalb der Tiefgaragenebene und schließt mit sechs Obergeschossen an das bestehende, hintere Eckgebäude Claire-Waldoff-Straße 5 an. In Richtung Reinhardtstraße wird die Geschossigkeit wegen der Abstandsflächen zum Nachbarn Reinhardtstraße 6 sukzessive bis auf zwei Geschosse und Dachterrasse reduziert. Der Anschluss zwischen der 6-geschossigen Aufstockung und der Claire-Waldoff-Straße 5 wird nicht als geschlossener Bau hergestellt. Offene, aufeinandergestapelte, "luftige" Terrassenetagen in Stahlbetonbauweise schaffen eine licht- und luftumspülte Verbindung, die eine neue Qualität auf dem Grundstück herstellt und den zukünftigen Bewohnern des Altbaus zu Gute kommt.

title: Germany – Woodwork – Grundschule Wagenstadt - Zimmererarbeiten
description: Die Grundschule Herbolzheim‑Wagenstadt wurde in den 1960er‑Jahren errichtet und besteht aus einem dreigeschossigen Hauptgebäude ohne Unterkellerung. Westlich des Hauptgebäudes wurde im Jahr 1998 ein eingeschossiger Erweiterungsbau realisiert; gleichzeitig wurden Umbaumaßnahmen im Hauptgebäude durchgeführt. Die Grundschule wird über einen Zeitraum von ca. 1½ Jahren umfassend umgebaut und saniert. Das Bestandsgebäude erhält ein zusätzliches Dachgeschoss mit Satteldach sowie ein vollflächiges Wärmedämmverbundsystem mit vorgehängter Fassade. Die Dachkonstruktionen des Bestandsgebäudes sowie der Neubauten sind als vorgefertigte Dachelemente geplant und so auszuführen, dass die Elemente direkt per Kran an ihren jeweiligen Einbauort gehoben und montiert werden können. Das Gebäude wird bis auf den Rohbau vollständig entkernt und anschließend saniert. Südlich des Bestandsgebäudes wird ein neuer Anbau in Stahlbetonbauweise errichtet. Im Gebäudeinneren wird ein neuer Aufzug über alle Geschosse (Erdgeschoss bis 2. Obergeschoss) eingebaut. Für die erforderlichen Aushubarbeiten ist südlich und östlich des Bestandsgebäudes eine Verbaulösung vorgesehen. Nördlich des Bestandsgebäudes entsteht ein neues Treppenhaus in Stahlbetonbauweise, das als zweiter baulicher Rettungsweg dient. Der Zugang zum neuen Dachgeschoss erfolgt über dieses Treppenhaus. Beide Anbauten sind nicht unterkellert und erhalten eine Pfahlgründung. Bei der Herstellung der Baugruben ist die Grundbruchsicherheit des Bestandsgebäudes zwingend zu berücksichtigen. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind Zimmererarbeiten für die Sanierung und Erweiterung der Grundschule Wagenstadt in Herbolzheim. Die Leistungen umfassen Schadstoffsanierungs-, Rückbau- und Demontagearbeiten an bestehenden Dachaufbauten sowie die Herstellung von Holztragwerken für Sattel-, Pult- und Flachdächer, Giebelwandkonstruktionen, Dämm-, Beplankungs- und Ausbauarbeiten einschließlich zugehöriger Dachaufbauten und Nebenleistungen. description: Deze Europese aanbesteding heeft betrekking op het planmatig en projectmatig onderhoud van natuur, terreinen en bijbehorende infrastructuur binnen de door Dunea beheerde gebieden. De opdracht omvat werkzaamheden in de duingebieden, natuurterreinen en productielocaties van Dunea, met als doel de instandhouding van natuurwaarden, recreatieve voorzieningen en een veilige leefomgeving te waarborgen. De werkzaamheden variëren van regulier onderhoud tot specialistische natuurbeheermaatregelen en projecten. Daarnaast omvat de opdracht onder meer bosbeheer, maaiwerkzaamheden, bestrijding van invasieve exoten, afrasteringen, recreatieve voorzieningen en terreinonderhoud op productielocaties. Dunea zoekt hiervoor professionele partners die beschikken over de benodigde kennis, capaciteit en expertise om deze werkzaamheden duurzaam en veilig uit te voeren. Met deze aanbesteding beoogt Dunea de continuïteit, kwaliteit en beheersbaarheid van het onderhoud voor de komende jaren te borgen en de afhankelijkheid van een beperkt aantal marktpartijen te verminderen. Duurzaamheid, samenwerking, veiligheid en kwaliteit vormen daarbij belangrijke uitgangspunten. De opdracht wordt in meerdere percelen aanbesteed, zodat gespecialiseerde marktpartijen kunnen inschrijven op het deel van de werkzaamheden dat het beste aansluit bij hun expertise. Inschrijvers worden uitgenodigd om aan te tonen hoe zij bijdragen aan een toekomstbestendig beheer van de natuur- en terreinwaarden binnen het werkgebied van Dunea.

title: Sweden – Library software package – Bibliotekssystem och webbplats

Syftet med upphandlingen är att säkerställa en långsiktigt hållbar, flexibel och användarvänlig digital infrastruktur som stödjer biblioteken i Ekerös uppdrag att främja läsning, kunskap, delaktighet och demokrati. Bibliotekssystemet och tillhörande publik webbplats ska möta dagens och framtidens behov hos invånare, besökare och medarbetare enligt Bilaga – Kravspecifikation. Kultur- och fritidsförvaltningen i Ekerö kommun är beställare och mottagare av det upphandlade systemet. Nuläge Kultur- och fritidsförvaltningen i Ekerö kommun använder idag bibliotekssystemet Book-IT och den integrerade webbplatsen Axiell Arena Nova. Ekerö kommun uppskattar att cirka 25 medarbetare inom kultur- och fritidsförvaltningen använder systemet och webbplatsen idag. Antalet biblioteksanvändare i bibliotekssystemet idag är cirka 4000 inom skolbiblioteksverksamheten och cirka 10 000 inom folkbiblioteksverksamheten. Antalet besök på den publika webbplatsen uppskattas till cirka 100 000 om året och sker från både mobiltelefon och dator. Tidplan Ekerö kommun planerar att tilldela upphandlingen i november 2026 och har som krav att ett nytt bibliotekssystem med tillhörande installation, migrering och implementation ska vara fullt fungerande och i drift senast 15 mars 2027.

title: Movement Area Guidance Signs (MAGS)
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific (NAVFAC Pacific) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to identify potential manufacturers capable of producing movement area guidance signs (MAGS) that have equal performance and listing/approval requirements as the ADB Safegate MAGS (Model: Reliance) that is manufactured by ADB Safegate. Responses from third-party distributors, pass-through resellers, or supply brokers who do not directly own the production line or manufacturing rights to a qualified equivalent product will not be considered responsive to this market survey. FY26 Project WWXT240800 Multi-Purpose Apron and Taxiway, located on Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Base Tindal (TDL), Australia requires MAGS that demonstrate the following salient characteristics: Character form and dimensions Dimensions as per DASDRM Section 6 Body to have minimum 150mm ground clearance Where multiple panels required, inscription colour and face to appear continuous over any joint. No intensity change or bars at any joint. Inscription character form and dimension as per DASDRM Section 6 Lighting methods Must operate on a series circuit common with taxiway lights Must operate over entire range of currents required for taxiway lights (typically between 2.8A and 6.6A) Sign colour Inscription and background colour in conformity with ICAO Annex 14 Each sign panel must match adjacent sign panels Colour of all signs must precisely match Sign luminance Must operate uniformly with taxiway lights when on a common circuit Luminance ratio between different coloured elements of a sign must not be greater than 1:10 No light output from black areas of the inscription or body LED modules and wiring LED modules must be easily and readily available Must be available on short delivery Must be robust and suitable for aviation purposes Must operate within the current range associated with the taxiway lights (2.8-6-6A) Must include surge protection Must be supplied from a series isolating transformer Construction Capable of withstanding vibrating wind force as per Part 139 MOS Frangible mounting Not exceed the maximum height specified in Part 139 MOS This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify potential alternative MAGS that will satisfy agency requirements. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data in order for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c)(2), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please submit complete information via email to Ms. Josie Damo-Agcaoili via electronic mail at josie.g.damo-agcaoili.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 06 October 2026 at 12:00 p.m. H.S.T. Information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property and will not be returned. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.

title: G001--Cremation and related services for unclaimed remains Portland VAMC
description: Notice of Sources Sought The purpose of this Sources Sought Announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Businesses (VOSB), Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) and Small Businesses interested and capable of providing the services requested, as well as any large businesses. The results from this source sought notice will be used to determine the appropriate set-aside. The intended contract is a firm-fixed price service contract. The SBA Non-Manufacturer Rule is not applicable as the intended contract is for services. The Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO20 is looking for manufacturer authorized service providers with access to OEM parts of the following requirement: Cremation and other services for unclaimed remains of veterans for Portland VAMC in accordance with the Statement of Work. Estimated quantity is for 10 decedents per year. Base + 4 Option Years Removal/transportation (Clark, Multnomah, Clackamas and Washington Counties around Portland, OR metro) Storage Cremation services Discharge handling State filing Discharge Statement of Work: The VA Portland Health Care System (VAPORHCS) provides comprehensive health care services to Veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces. As part of this mission, VA administers decedent affairs, ensuring that the handling of Veteran remains is conducted with dignity, respect, and compassionate support for families, staff, and the community. The VA requires contracted support to assist with decedent services, including the transportation of remains, preparation for burial or cremation, and coordination of final disposition for unclaimed remains. These services are essential to ensure timely, respectful, and compliant handling of decedents entrusted to the VA. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, vehicles, supplies, and facilities necessary to perform the decedent services described in this Statement of Work. PURPOSE/GENERAL DESCRIPTION/TASKS The purpose of this requirement is to support the (VAPORHCS) in the dignified and timely handling of Veteran decedent affairs. These services ensure that the transport, preparation, and disposition of remains are conducted respectfully and in accordance with applicable VA policies The Contractor shall perform all work in accordance with federal, state, local laws and VA policies, including but not limited to VHA Directive 1601B.04, VHA Notice 2025-03 Survivors Assistance and Memorial Support, 38 U.S.C. §§ 2303 and 2308, 38 C.F.R. §§ 17.170, 3.1708, and 3.1709 and applicable funeral service regulations. The contractor shall provide all personnel, vehicles, equipment, supplies, and facilities necessary to perform decedent-related services as required by the VA. Tasks under this requirement generally include the pickup and transport of remains within the VA facility, transport to and from external medical facilities, transport to the contractor s facility for preparation, preparation of remains for cremation, provision of required containers, and delivery of remains to the Willamette National Cemetery. The contractor shall provide timely, reliable, and professional support to ensure proper handling and continuity of decedent services for unclaimed remains and others as directed by the VA. Pick up the deceased patient at the place of death within 2 business days after notification when climate controlled holding facilities are available. Pick up within 4 hours after notification when climate controlled holding facilities are not available . Emergent or unforeseen circumstances (e.g., morgue malfunction or shutdown) may require expedited pickup. In such cases, the contractor shall pick up the remains within 4 hours of being notified. Transport the body of the deceased to its place of business to prepare the body for cremation when ordered by the SAMS Specialist (Survivor Assistance and Memorial Support Specialist) AOD (Administrative Officer of the Day), or other VAPORHCS authorized approving official. Provide refrigerated storage for remains until cremation arrangements are completed. Cremation shall include making the necessary arrangements with the crematorium and furnishing a suitable urn for the cremated remains. Providing a suitable Urn shall be durable and sealed, not leaking. Material, such as plastic, metal, wood, ceramic/stone, or other durable materials are acceptable. Urn must be clearly labeled to allow for identification of remains without opening of containers. Remains designated for cremation shall be cremated without embalming unless otherwise instructed. The Contractor shall have the necessary vehicles and licensed operators to transport the body/remains from the (VAPORHCS) to the funeral home and then from funeral home to the National Cemetery for interment. Coordinate final disposition, including delivery of remains to authorized location for cremation and the National Cemetery for interment. Maintain chain-of-custody documentation for all transfers of remains. Assist with required documentation related to disposition, including coordination and filing of death certificates as directed by VHAPORHCS. The Contractor shall possess the current transit permit at the time of award of Contract. Permits covering removal of the body, if required, are to be secured and paid for by the Contractor. The Contractor s employees shall have the appropriate and current license(s) prior to commencing work under this contract. Copies of registrations and licenses shall be furnished upon SAMS request. Offerors must be an approved member of the Funeral Services Licensing facility under the Oregon and Washington Department of Health Services. 3.0 Government Responsibilities VA will: Notify Contractor of unclaimed remains. Conduct inspections of remains, facilities, and merchandise. title: Germany – Structural steelworks – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Stahlbauarbeiten
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Portugal – Research and development consultancy services – MASSIVE – Metabolite Analysis System Supporting In-depth Validation and Exploration
description: Regulation (EU) 2023/1322, which establishes the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA), strengthens the Union’s preparedness for, and response to, drug-related health and security challenges. Article 15 in particular provides for a dedicated network of forensic and toxicology laboratories to enhance analytical capacity, harmonise methods, support quality assurance and facilitate the exchange of data and expertise across Member States. This strengthens and supports the timely detection, assessment and response to drug-related risks. Within this policy context, systematic investigation of drug metabolism is a cornerstone of clinical and forensic toxicology. Overall, the objective of this contract is to reinforce collective capacity across the EU to interpret toxicological findings and, critically, to improve the detection, identification, and timely reporting of exposure to NPS and other illicit drugs. By generating robust metabolic, pharmacological, and analytical data, and by consolidating these outputs into a centralised, accessible EU database, the project aims to strengthen timely reporting, harmonise practices, and ensure that toxicological evidence can be translated more effectively into monitoring, early warning, and public health responses to emerging NPS threats.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE FOR BLM ARIZONA - Abandoned Mine Lands (AML) Biological Survey, Hazard Mitigation, and Closure Support to the Arizona Game and Fish Department (AGFD) THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Bureau of Land Management, Arizona State Office, intends to award a firm-fixed-price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, to: Arizona Game and Fish Department (AGFD) 5000 W. Carefree Highway Phoenix, AZ 85086 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 813312 (Environment, Conservation, and Wildlife Organizations). The Product Service Code (PSC) is F011 (Wildlife Conservation Services). BLM requires the Contractor to perform wildlife biological surveys, physical hazard assessments, mitigation activities, and closure of Abandoned Mine Land (AML) features located on BLM-managed public lands statewide. These features include shafts, adits, tunnels, declines, trenches, prospect cuts, and associated structures that pose significant threats to public safety. The requirement includes: � Biological surveys to evaluate bat and other wildlife habitat use at AML features. � Physical hazard assessment and prioritization. � Interim hazard mitigation (e.g., fencing, signage) consistent with BLM specifications. � Development of site-specific closure recommendations based on habitat value, physical hazard level, and regulatory compliance. � Support for permanent closures using approved methods such as backfill, polyurethane foam (PUF), cable-net installation, bat compatible gates, corrugated steel pipe (CSP), and cast in place concrete systems. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation. However, if any interested party believes it can meet the above requirement, it may submit a statement of capabilities.
